metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF→text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Learning with Errors (LWE) problem
nodes.statement: Given samples from $A_{s,\chi}$ on $\mathbb{Z}_p^n \times \mathbb{Z}_p$, where each sample is $(a, \langle s,a\rangle + e \bmod p)$ with $a \sim U(\mathbb{Z}_p^n)$ and $e \sim \chi$, recover $s \in \mathbb{Z}_p^n$. Denoted $\mathrm{LWE}_{p,\chi}$.
nodes.statement_clean: The LWE problem: recover a secret vector s in Z_p^n from many noisy linear equations <s,a_i> = b_i + e_i (mod p) where the noise e_i is drawn from distribution chi.

nodes.name: Discrete Gaussian distribution $D_{L,r}$
nodes.statement: For a countable set $A$ (typically a lattice) and $r > 0$, $D_{A,r}(x) := \rho_r(x) / \rho_r(A)$ where $\rho_r(x) = \exp(-\pi \| x/r \|^2)$ is the Gaussian function of width $r$.

nodes.name: Distribution $\Psi_\beta$ (periodic normal) and discretization $\bar\Psi_\alpha$
nodes.statement: $\Psi_\beta$ is the distribution on $\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ obtained by sampling a normal variable with mean 0 and standard deviation $\beta/\sqrt{2\pi}$ and reducing mod 1; $\bar\Psi_\alpha$ is its discretization to $\mathbb{Z}_p$ via Eq. (8): $\bar\phi(i) := \int_{(i-1/2)/p}^{(i+1/2)/p} \phi(x)\, dx$.

nodes.name: Distribution $A_{s,\chi}$
nodes.statement: For $s \in \mathbb{Z}_p^n$ and $\chi$ on $\mathbb{Z}_p$, $A_{s,\chi}$ samples $a \sim U(\mathbb{Z}_p^n)$ and $e \sim \chi$ and outputs $(a, \langle a, s\rangle + e) \in \mathbb{Z}_p^n \times \mathbb{Z}_p$.

nodes.name: Smoothing parameter $\eta_\varepsilon(L)$
nodes.statement: For an $n$-dimensional lattice $L$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, $\eta_\varepsilon(L)$ is the smallest $s$ such that $\rho_{1/s}(L^* \setminus \{0\}) \le \varepsilon$.
nodes.statement_clean: The smoothing parameter is the smallest scale at which the discrete Gaussian on a lattice 'looks like' a continuous one.

nodes.name: $\mathrm{GapSVP}_\gamma$
nodes.statement: An instance is an $n$-dimensional lattice $L$ and $d > 0$. YES: $\lambda_1(L) \le d$. NO: $\lambda_1(L) > \gamma(n) \cdot d$.
nodes.origin_citation: Standard lattice problem; see e.g. Micciancio-Goldwasser [28]

nodes.name: $\mathrm{SIVP}_\gamma$
nodes.statement: Given an $n$-dimensional lattice $L$, output $n$ linearly independent lattice vectors of length at most $\gamma(n) \cdot \lambda_n(L)$.

nodes.name: $\mathrm{GIVP}_\gamma^\varphi$
nodes.statement: Given an $n$-dimensional lattice $L$, output $n$ linearly independent lattice vectors of length at most $\gamma(n) \cdot \varphi(L)$. Choosing $\varphi = \lambda_n$ recovers SIVP.

nodes.name: Discrete Gaussian Sampling problem $\mathrm{DGS}^\varphi$
nodes.statement: Given an $n$-dimensional lattice $L$ and $r > \varphi(L)$, output a sample from $D_{L,r}$.

nodes.name: Bounded-distance $\mathrm{CVP}_{L,d}$
nodes.statement: Given a lattice $L$, $d > 0$ (with $d < \lambda_1(L)/2$ in this paper), and $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with $\mathrm{dist}(x, L) \le d$, find the (unique) closest lattice point $\kappa_L(x)$.

nodes.name: $\mathrm{CVP}^{(p)}_{L,d}$ (closest-vector coefficients mod $p$)
nodes.statement: Given $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ within distance $d$ of $L$, output $L^{-1} \kappa_L(x) \bmod p \in \mathbb{Z}_p^n$, the coefficient vector of the closest lattice point reduced modulo $p$.

nodes.name: $\mathrm{GapCVP}_\gamma$ and $\mathrm{GapCVP}'_\gamma$
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{GapCVP}_\gamma$: input $(L, t, d)$; YES if $\mathrm{dist}(t,L) \le d$, NO if $\mathrm{dist}(t,L) > \gamma(n) d$. $\mathrm{GapCVP}'_\gamma$: NO instances additionally require $\lambda_1(L) > \gamma(n) d$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.1 (Informal main theorem)
nodes.statement: Let $n,p$ be integers and $\alpha \in (0,1)$ with $\alpha p > 2\sqrt{n}$. If there is an efficient algorithm for $\mathrm{LWE}_{p,\bar\Psi_\alpha}$ then there is an efficient quantum algorithm approximating $\mathrm{GapSVP}$ and $\mathrm{SIVP}$ to within $\tilde O(n/\alpha)$ in the worst case.
conclusions: Efficient quantum algorithm approximating worst-case $\mathrm{GapSVP}$ and $\mathrm{SIVP}$ to within $\tilde O(n/\alpha)$

nodes.name: Theorem 3.1 (Main theorem, formal)
nodes.statement: Let $\varepsilon = \varepsilon(n)$ be negligible, $p = p(n)$ an integer and $\alpha \in (0,1)$ with $\alpha p > 2\sqrt{n}$. Given an oracle $W$ solving $\mathrm{LWE}_{p, \Psi_\alpha}$ from polynomially many samples, there is an efficient quantum algorithm for $\mathrm{DGS}_{\sqrt{2n}\cdot \eta_\varepsilon(L)/\alpha}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.3 (Banaszczyk transference)
nodes.statement: For any $n$-dimensional lattice $L$, $1 \le \lambda_1(L) \cdot \lambda_n(L^*) \le n$.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.4 (Banaszczyk Gaussian-mass scaling)
nodes.statement: For any lattice $L$ and $a \ge 1$, $\rho_a(L) \le a^n \rho(L)$.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.5 (Banaszczyk tail bound)
nodes.statement: For any lattice $L$ and $r > 0$, $\rho_r(L \setminus \sqrt{n} r B_n) < 2^{-2n} \cdot \rho_r(L)$, i.e. lattice points of norm $> \sqrt{n} r$ carry exponentially small Gaussian mass.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.11 (smoothing-parameter upper bound via $\lambda_1(L^*)$)
nodes.statement: For any $n$-dimensional lattice $L$, $\eta_\varepsilon(L) \le \sqrt{n}/\lambda_1(L^*)$ where $\varepsilon = 2^{-n}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.12 (smoothing-parameter upper bound via $\lambda_n$)
nodes.statement: For any lattice $L$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, $\eta_\varepsilon(L) \le \sqrt{\ln(2n(1+1/\varepsilon))/\pi} \cdot \lambda_n(L)$. In particular for any $\omega(\log n)$, $\eta_{\varepsilon(n)}(L) \le \sqrt{\omega(\log n)} \cdot \lambda_n(L)$ for some negligible $\varepsilon(n)$.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.14 (Poisson summation formula)
nodes.statement: For any lattice $L$ and any function $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{C}$, $f(L) = \det(L^*) \hat f(L^*)$.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.2 (Bootstrapping)
nodes.statement: There exists an efficient algorithm that, given any $n$-dimensional lattice $L$ and $r > 2^{2n} \lambda_n(L)$, outputs a sample from a distribution within statistical distance $2^{-\Omega(n)}$ of $D_{L,r}$.
conclusions: Efficient sampler within statistical distance $2^{-\Omega(n)}$ of $D_{L,r}$

nodes.name: Lemma 3.3 (Iterative step)
nodes.statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem 3.1, there is a constant $c > 0$ and an efficient quantum algorithm that, given an $n$-dim lattice $L$, $r > \sqrt{2} p\, \eta_\varepsilon(L)$, and $n^c$ samples from $D_{L,r}$, produces a sample from $D_{L, r\sqrt{n}/(\alpha p)}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.4 (First part of iterative step)
nodes.statement: Under the LWE oracle assumption, given $L$, $r > \sqrt{2} p\, \eta_\varepsilon(L)$, and $n^c$ samples from $D_{L,r}$, there is an efficient classical algorithm solving $\mathrm{CVP}_{L^*, \alpha p / (\sqrt{2} r)}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.5 (Coefficients-mod-$p$ suffice for CVP)
nodes.statement: There is an efficient algorithm that, given $L$, $d < \lambda_1(L)/2$, and $p \ge 2$, solves $\mathrm{CVP}_{L,d}$ given oracle access to $\mathrm{CVP}^{(p)}_{L,d}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.6 (Verifying solutions of LWE)
nodes.statement: There is an efficient algorithm that, given $s'$ and samples from $A_{s,\Psi_\alpha}$ for unknown $s$ and $\alpha < 1$, decides whether $s = s'$ correctly with probability exponentially close to 1.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.7 (Handling error $\Psi_\beta$ for $\beta \le \alpha$)
nodes.statement: Given an oracle $W$ for $\mathrm{LWE}_{p,\Psi_\alpha}$, there is an efficient algorithm $W'$ that on input samples from $A_{s,\Psi_\beta}$ for any unknown $\beta \le \alpha$ outputs $s$ with probability exponentially close to 1.

nodes.name: Claim 2.1 (Local stability of $\rho_s$)
nodes.statement: For all $s, t, l > 0$ and $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with $\| x \| \le t$ and $\| x - y \| \le l$, $\rho_s(y) \ge (1 - \pi(2lt + l^2)/s^2) \rho_s(x)$.

nodes.name: Claim 2.2 (Stability of $\Psi_\beta$ in $\beta$)
nodes.statement: For any $0 < \alpha < \beta \le 2\alpha$, $\Delta(\Psi_\alpha, \Psi_\beta) \le 9 (\beta/\alpha - 1)$.

nodes.name: Claim 2.13 (Smoothing-parameter lower bound)
nodes.statement: For any lattice $L$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, $\eta_\varepsilon(L) \ge \sqrt{\ln(1/\varepsilon)/\pi} \cdot 1/\lambda_1(L^*) \ge \sqrt{\ln(1/\varepsilon)/\pi} \cdot \lambda_n(L)/n$.

nodes.name: Claim 3.8 (Shift-invariance above smoothing parameter)
nodes.statement: For any lattice $L$, $c \in \mathbb{R}^n$, $\varepsilon > 0$, and $r \ge \eta_\varepsilon(L)$: $\rho_r(L + c) \in r^n \det(L^*) (1 \pm \varepsilon)$.

nodes.name: Claim 3.9 (Discrete + continuous Gaussian \u2248 wider continuous Gaussian)
nodes.statement: Let $t = \sqrt{r^2 + s^2}$ with $rs/t \ge \eta_\varepsilon(L)$, $\varepsilon < 1/2$. Sampling from $D_{L+u,r}$ then adding $\nu_s$ noise yields a distribution within statistical distance $4\varepsilon$ of $\nu_t$.

nodes.name: Corollary 3.10 (Inner-product noise after discrete-Gaussian sampling)
nodes.statement: Under $1/\sqrt{1/r^2 + (\| z\|/\alpha)^2} \ge \eta_\varepsilon(L)$, the distribution of $\langle z, v \rangle + e \bmod 1$ (with $v \sim D_{L+u,r}$, $e$ normal of std $\alpha/\sqrt{2\pi}$) is within statistical distance $4\varepsilon$ of $\Psi_{\sqrt{(r\| z\|)^2 + \alpha^2}}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.11 (Main procedure of the first part)
nodes.statement: Under the (variable-$\beta$) LWE oracle, given $L$, $r > \sqrt{2}p\, \eta_\varepsilon(L)$, and a polynomial number of samples from $D_{L,r}$, an efficient algorithm solves $\mathrm{CVP}^{(p)}_{L^*, \alpha p / (\sqrt{2} r)}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.12 (Discrete quantum Gaussian state)
nodes.statement: There is an efficient quantum algorithm that, given $L \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^n$ and $r > 2^{2n} \lambda_n(L)$, outputs a state within $\ell_2$ distance $2^{-\Omega(n)}$ of the normalized $\sum_{x \in L} \sqrt{\rho_r(x)} | x \rangle$.

nodes.name: Claim 3.13 (Quantum-state-mod-$P(L)$ approximation)
nodes.statement: For $R \ge 1$ integer and lattice $L$ with $\lambda_1(L) > 2\sqrt{n}$, the $\ell_2$ distance between the normalized states $|\vartheta_1\rangle = \sum_{x \in L/R, \|x\| < \sqrt{n}} \rho(x) |x \bmod P(L)\rangle$ and $|\vartheta_2\rangle = \sum_{x \in L/R} \rho(x) | x \bmod P(L)\rangle$ is $2^{-\Omega(n)}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.14 (Second part of iterative step)
nodes.statement: There is an efficient quantum algorithm that, given $L$, $d < \lambda_1(L^*)/2$, and an oracle for $\mathrm{CVP}_{L^*, d}$, outputs a sample from $D_{L, \sqrt{n}/(\sqrt{2} d)}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.15 (Discrete Gaussian escapes any subspace)
nodes.statement: For any $n$-dim lattice $L$ and $r \ge \sqrt{2}\, \eta_\varepsilon(L)$ with $\varepsilon \le 1/10$, and any subspace $H$ of dimension at most $n-1$, $\Pr_{x \sim D_{L,r}}[x \notin H] \ge 1/10$.

nodes.name: Corollary 3.16 ($n^2$ DGS samples span $\mathbb{R}^n$)
nodes.statement: Under the conditions of Lemma 3.15, the probability that $n^2$ independent samples from $D_{L,r}$ contain no $n$ linearly independent vectors is exponentially small.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.17 (Reduction GIVP $\to$ DGS)
nodes.statement: For any $\varepsilon \le 1/10$ and any $\varphi(L) \ge \sqrt{2}\, \eta_\varepsilon(L)$, there is a polynomial-time reduction from $\mathrm{GIVP}_{2\sqrt{n}\varphi}$ to $\mathrm{DGS}^\varphi$.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.20 (Reduction GapCVP$'$ $\to$ DGS)
nodes.statement: For any $\gamma(n) \ge 1$, there is a polynomial-time reduction from $\mathrm{GapCVP}'_{100\sqrt{n}\,\gamma(n)}$ to $\mathrm{DGS}_{\sqrt{n}\,\gamma(n)/\lambda_1(L^*)}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.1 (Average-case to worst-case for LWE-decision)
nodes.statement: If $W$ distinguishes $A_{s,\chi}$ from $U$ for a non-negligible fraction of $s$, then there is an efficient algorithm $W'$ that for all $s$ accepts $A_{s,\chi}$ and rejects $U$ with probability exponentially close to 1.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.2 (Decision to search)
nodes.statement: For prime $p \le \mathrm{poly}(n)$ and any $\chi$ on $\mathbb{Z}_p$: a procedure that for all $s$ distinguishes $A_{s,\chi}$ from $U$ implies an efficient algorithm that on samples from $A_{s,\chi}$ recovers $s$ w.h.p.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.3 (Discrete to continuous LWE)
nodes.statement: If $W$ solves $\mathrm{LWE}_{p,\bar\phi}$ then there is an efficient algorithm $W'$ that solves $\mathrm{LWE}_{p,\phi}$ (just discretize the second coordinate of each sample).

nodes.name: Lemma 4.4 (Distinguisher implies LWE solver)
nodes.statement: For prime $p \le \mathrm{poly}(n)$, $\phi$ a density on $\mathbb{T}$ and $\bar\phi$ its discretization: a distinguisher of $A_{s,\bar\phi}$ from $U$ for a non-negligible fraction of $s$ implies an efficient algorithm solving $\mathrm{LWE}_{p,\phi}$.

nodes.name: Discrete Gaussian Sampling (DGS)
nodes.statement: Given an $n$-dim lattice $L$ and $r > \varphi(L)$ for some lattice function $\varphi$, output a sample from $D_{L,r}$. Used as the central reduction target.

nodes.name: Public-key cryptosystem (LWE-based)
nodes.statement: Build an IND-CPA public-key cryptosystem with private key $s \in \mathbb{Z}_p^n$, public key $(a_i, b_i)_{i=1}^m$ with $b_i = \langle a_i, s\rangle + e_i$ ($e_i \sim \chi$), encrypting bits via subset sums.

nodes.name: DGS algorithm via iterative step (proof of Theorem 3.1)
nodes.statement: Quantum algorithm for $\mathrm{DGS}_{\sqrt{2n}\eta_\varepsilon(L)/\alpha}$: bootstrap to $D_{L,r_{3n}}$, then for $i = 3n, \ldots, 1$ apply the iterative step (Lemma 3.3) $n^c$ times to step down from $D_{L,r_i}$ to $D_{L,r_{i-1}}$; output one sample from $D_{L,r_0} = D_{L,r}$.

nodes.name: Iterative step (Lemma 3.3 procedure)
nodes.statement: Combines a classical part (Lemma 3.4: samples + LWE oracle $\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{CVP}_{L^*, \alpha p/(\sqrt 2 r)}$) with a quantum part (Lemma 3.14: CVP oracle $\Rightarrow$ sample from $D_{L, r\sqrt{n}/(\alpha p)}$).
output: One sample from $D_{L, r\sqrt n/(\alpha p)}$

nodes.name: Regev LWE-based public-key cryptosystem
nodes.statement: Encrypt a bit $c$ by choosing a random subset $S \subseteq [m]$ and outputting $(\sum_S a_i, \sum_S b_i)$ for $c = 0$ or $(\sum_S a_i, \lfloor p/2\rfloor + \sum_S b_i)$ for $c = 1$. Decrypt $(a, b)$ as $0$ if $b - \langle a, s\rangle$ is closer to $0$ than to $\lfloor p/2\rfloor$ mod $p$, else $1$.

nodes.name: Claim 5.2 (Noise sums stay small)
nodes.statement: For the chosen parameters, $\Pr_{e \sim \bar\Psi_\alpha^{\star k}}[ |e| < \lfloor p/2\rfloor /2 ] > 1 - \delta(n)$ for some negligible $\delta(n)$, all $k \in \{0,\ldots,m\}$.

nodes.name: Claim 5.3 (Leftover-hash-style mixing)
nodes.statement: For finite Abelian group $G$ and $l \in \mathbb{N}$: the expected statistical distance between $U(G)$ and the distribution of a random subset-sum of $g_1,\ldots,g_l$ over uniform $g_i$ is at most $\sqrt{|G|/2^l}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 5.1 (Correctness)
nodes.statement: If $\Pr_{e \sim \chi^{\star k}}[|e| < \lfloor p/2\rfloor/2] > 1 - \delta$ for all $k \in \{0,\ldots,m\}$, then the cryptosystem's decryption error probability is at most $\delta$.

nodes.name: Lemma 5.4 (Security: distinguisher reduction)
nodes.statement: For any $\varepsilon > 0$ and $m \ge (1+\varepsilon)(n+1)\log p$: a polynomial-time distinguisher between encryptions of 0 and 1 yields a distinguisher between $A_{s,\chi}$ and $U$ for a non-negligible fraction of $s$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.1
nodes.statement: By induction down a geometric scale: bootstrap to a very wide DGS, then apply the iterative step $3n$ times, each time shrinking the width by a factor $\alpha p/\sqrt{n} > 2$.

nodes.name: Set up width sequence and bootstrap
nodes.statement: Let $r_i := r \cdot (\alpha p/\sqrt n)^i$. Apply Lemma 3.2 to produce $n^c$ samples from $D_{L, r_{3n}}$ (legal since $r_{3n} > 2^{2n}\lambda_n(L)$ by Claim 2.13).

nodes.name: Iterate the iterative step $3n$ times
nodes.statement: For $i = 3n, 3n-1, \ldots, 1$ apply Lemma 3.3 $n^c$ times to convert $n^c$ samples from $D_{L,r_i}$ into $n^c$ samples from $D_{L,r_{i-1}}$. The condition $r_i \ge \sqrt{2} p\, \eta_\varepsilon(L)$ holds for all $i \ge 1$.

nodes.name: Output a sample from $D_{L,r}$
nodes.statement: After the loop we hold $n^c$ samples from $D_{L, r_0} = D_{L,r}$; output the first one.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.3 (iterative step)
nodes.statement: Two-part construction: classical $\mathrm{CVP}_{L^*, \alpha p/(\sqrt 2 r)}$ algorithm via Lemma 3.4, then quantum sampling via Lemma 3.14.

nodes.name: Classical CVP from samples + LWE (Lemma 3.4)
nodes.statement: Use the input samples and the LWE oracle to solve $\mathrm{CVP}_{L^*, \alpha p/(\sqrt 2 r)}$ classically.

nodes.name: Quantum sampling from CVP oracle (Lemma 3.14)
nodes.statement: Use the resulting CVP oracle quantumly to produce a sample from $D_{L, r\sqrt n/(\alpha p)}$. The condition $\alpha p/(\sqrt 2 r) \le \lambda_1(L^*)/2$ is met by Claim 2.13.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.11 (samples + LWE $\to$ CVP$^{(p)}$)
nodes.statement: Given $x$ within distance $\alpha p/(\sqrt 2 r)$ of $L^*$, sample $v \sim D_{L,r}$, set $a = L^{-1} v \bmod p$, output $(a, \langle x, v\rangle/p + e \bmod 1)$ with Gaussian $e$. Show this is statistically close to $A_{s, \Psi_\beta}$ with $s = (L^*)^{-1}\kappa_{L^*}(x) \bmod p$ and some $\beta \le \alpha$, then call $W'$ from Lemma 3.7.

nodes.name: Marginal of $a$ is essentially uniform
nodes.statement: Each $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p^n$ has probability $\propto \rho_r(pL + La) = (r/p)^n \det(L^*)(1 \pm \varepsilon)$ by Claim 3.8 with $\eta_\varepsilon(pL) = p \eta_\varepsilon(L) < r$, so $a$'s distribution is negligibly close to uniform.

nodes.name: Linear-equation form mod 1
nodes.statement: Decompose $\langle x, v\rangle/p + e \bmod 1 = \langle x'/p, v\rangle + e + \langle \kappa_{L^*}(x), v\rangle/p$ with $x' = x - \kappa_{L^*}(x)$; the last term equals $\langle s, a\rangle/p \bmod 1$.

nodes.name: Noise is statistically close to $\Psi_\beta$ with $\beta \le \alpha$
nodes.statement: Apply Corollary 3.10 to $\langle x'/p, v\rangle + e$ to bound its statistical distance from $\Psi_\beta$ for $\beta = \sqrt{(r\| x'\|/p)^2 + \alpha^2/2} \le \alpha$.

nodes.name: Recover $s$ via Lemma 3.7
nodes.statement: Feed the resulting $A_{s, \Psi_\beta}$ samples to algorithm $W'$ from Lemma 3.7 (which handles unknown $\beta \le \alpha$) to recover $s = (L^*)^{-1}\kappa_{L^*}(x) \bmod p$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.14 (CVP $\to$ DGS via QFT)
nodes.statement: Quantum: prepare a discrete Gaussian state on $L^*/R$ via Lemma 3.12; reduce mod $P(L^*)$ and uncompute the first register using the CVP oracle; apply the quantum Fourier transform on $\mathbb{Z}_R^n$; measure to obtain a sample from $D_{L, 1/\sqrt 2}$ (so by scaling, from $D_{L, \sqrt n/(\sqrt 2 d)}$).

nodes.name: Build discrete-Gaussian quantum state on $L^*/R$
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 3.12 with $r = 1/\sqrt 2$ and lattice $L^*/R$ to obtain $\sum_{x \in L^*/R} \rho(x) |x\rangle$ (after Lemma 2.5 truncation).

nodes.name: Reduce mod $P(L^*)$ and uncompute via CVP
nodes.statement: Compute $x \bmod P(L^*)$ in a new register, then use the CVP oracle to recover $x$ and uncompute the first register, leaving $\sum \rho(x) | x \bmod P(L^*)\rangle$. Apply Claim 3.13.

nodes.name: Quantum Fourier transform on $\mathbb{Z}_R^n$
nodes.statement: Apply QFT; the resulting amplitude at $|t\rangle$ is $\propto \det(RL) \sum_{y \in RL} \rho(y - Lt)$ (using Lemma 2.14 and Eq. (10)).

nodes.name: Measure and decode via Babai
nodes.statement: Measure to get $x \bmod P(RL)$ for some $x \in L$, $\| x\| < \sqrt n$. Recover $x$ using Babai's nearest-plane algorithm; the output distribution is exponentially close to $D_{L, 1/\sqrt 2}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.4 (security reduction)
nodes.statement: From a distinguisher $W$ between encryptions of 0 and 1, build a distinguisher $W'$ between $A_{s,\chi}$ and $U$ for a $1/\mathrm{poly}(n)$ fraction of $s$, using Claim 5.3 (subset-sum mixing).

nodes.name: Why quantum?
nodes.statement: Quantum is needed in only one step of the main reduction: erasing a register that holds a (CVP-computed) lattice point in a unitary way. Classically, no analogous use of the bounded-distance CVP oracle is known.

nodes.name: Followup: classical reduction by Peikert
nodes.statement: Peikert [33] removes the quantum step, yielding a classical reduction $\mathrm{GapSVP} \to \mathrm{LWE}$, but at the cost of giving up the iterative structure, SIVP-hardness, and a polynomial modulus $p$.

nodes.name: Dequantize Theorem 1.1
nodes.statement: Can the hardness of LWE be based on the classical (rather than quantum) hardness of SIVP and GapSVP, with the same parameter regime?

nodes.name: Hardness of LPN ($p=2$)
nodes.statement: Establish lattice-based hardness of the learning-from-parity-with-errors problem (the case $p = 2$); the present theorem requires $p > 2\sqrt n$.
